title: The Biggest Race

pages.text: Mia wanted to enter the biggest race in the whole town more than anything else.
pages.scene: A young girl looking at a poster advertising a big town race.

pages.text: She had been running every morning and getting faster each day for many weeks.
pages.scene: Mia jogging through a park at sunrise, looking determined.

pages.text: Her older brother Alex was taller and had longer legs, but she never stopped trying.
pages.scene: Mia and her taller brother stretching together before practice.

pages.text: "Running takes practice," Alex reminded her as they stretched their tired muscles together.
pages.scene: Both siblings doing warm-up stretches on a grassy field.

pages.text: Mia nodded and started jogging faster, her feet pounding against the hard packed trail.
pages.scene: Mia running on a dirt trail, dust kicking up behind her.

pages.text: The morning of the race arrived, and runners from all the nearby towns gathered together.
pages.scene: A crowded starting line with runners of all ages stretching.

pages.text: Mia looked at the other racers and noticed some were bigger and looked much stronger.
pages.scene: Mia observing other competitors, some looking more athletic.

pages.text: She reminded herself that she had trained harder than ever before and was truly ready.
pages.scene: Mia taking a deep breath at the starting line, focused.

pages.text: The starting horn sounded and all the runners dashed forward at the very same moment.
pages.scene: Runners bursting from the starting line in a blur of motion.

pages.text: Mia started slower than the others but kept a steady pace without rushing too much.
pages.scene: Mia running at the back of the pack, calm expression.

pages.text: As the racers rounded the first corner, some tired runners began slowing down already.
pages.scene: Some runners slowing and breathing hard around a corner.

pages.text: Mia passed them easily because she had trained smarter and saved her best energy.
pages.scene: Mia passing tired runners, moving up in the pack.

pages.text: The fastest runners were still far ahead, but Mia kept pushing and never stopped.
pages.scene: Mia in the middle of the pack, leaders visible ahead.

pages.text: Her legs burned and her lungs ached, but she remembered all her morning practices.
pages.scene: Mia showing effort but determination on her face mid-race.

pages.text: She passed more racers as they slowed, and she moved into the top ten runners.
pages.scene: Mia advancing through the field, spectators cheering.

pages.text: The finish line appeared ahead, and Mia spotted Alex cheering and jumping in the crowd.
pages.scene: The finish line visible, Alex waving excitedly from the sidelines.

pages.text: Mia pushed harder than she ever had before, her arms pumping and legs flying.
pages.scene: Mia sprinting with everything she has toward the finish line.

pages.text: She crossed the finish line in fifth place, her best result in any race ever.
pages.scene: Mia crossing the finish line, arms raised in triumph.

pages.text: Alex rushed over and hugged her tightly, saying she was the bravest runner there.
pages.scene: Alex hugging Mia, both smiling broadly.

pages.text: "You trained harder and ran smarter than all those faster kids," Alex told her proudly.
pages.scene: Alex handing Mia water, speaking encouragingly.

pages.text: Mia smiled because she learned that being the biggest or fastest is not everything.
pages.scene: Mia looking content, holding her participation ribbon.

pages.text: Working harder and never quitting mattered most, and that made her the happiest racer today.
pages.scene: Mia standing on a small platform receiving a medal.

pages.text: She promised herself that she would keep training and racing for many more wonderful years.
pages.scene: Mia and Alex walking home together at sunset, talking happily.

pages.text: And the next year, Mia entered the same race and finished even higher than before.
pages.scene: Mia crossing a finish line with a huge smile, holding up three fingers for third place.
